intended_object: The standard homomorphism Sol ⋊ D₄ → Isom(Sol). A pair (p, g) is sent to the isometry q ↦ p · g(q): first apply the dihedral isometry g, which fixes the identity, then translate on the left by p. This is the usual description of the isometry group of Sol (Scott 1983, §4). The intended object comes from the docstring, the module documentation and the later use in `semidirectProductIsomMulEquiv`.
explanation:
The definition applies Mathlib's `SemidirectProduct.lift` to two maps:
- `toIsom : Sol →* Isom Sol`, which sends p to left multiplication by p;
- `dihedralToIsom : D₄ →* Isom Sol`, built from the reflection (x, y, z) ↦ (x, −y, z) and the swap (x, y, z) ↦ (y, x, −z).

The compatibility condition is that conjugating a translation by g gives the translation by g(p). This holds because each dihedral isometry is also a group automorphism of Sol, which is what `dihedralMulAut` records. The proved lemma `semidirectProductToIsom_apply` gives (p, g) ↦ (q ↦ p · g(q)), which is the standard formula.

The library also proves the map is injective, and in the Classification file that it is bijective. So it matches the textbook identification Isom(Sol) ≅ Sol ⋊ D₄.

This is a specific map on a specific geometry, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no counterpart: it does not define Sol or its isometry group.
